html:
In the app

File → New Project… → A graded level → 4. Guided mode opens on this chapter: the tags, every rung below under its fold, a Verify check, and the run results: the roller comes in and PadIn answers, a bottle leaves with a label, the roll runs out and a new one is loaded, then complete, every bottle right and under par. File → Load Reference Solution loads the program printed here.

On the bottle line (chapter 27) the labeler is one station among many, and its handshake is written in two rungs between the capper and the scrap gate. This level is the labeler alone, so you can see the whole of it: what the dispenser tells you, what it wants from you, and what goes wrong when the roll runs out. Twenty-four bottles come down a short belt, filled and capped but with no label, and about a fifth of them with no cap at all. Every capped bottle has to leave with a label; the uncapped ones get none and go to the reject bin. The roll holds sixteen labels, which is not enough: somewhere past bottle twenty the dispenser runs dry, and the program has to stop feeding bottles into it until the operator loads a new roll.

The hopper is a timing-screw infeed with its own screen, the pusher a guided cylinder squared up with its eye (both in the Real models section of the simulator chapter). A level you saved in an older version keeps its scene in your browser; when a level’s layout changes between versions the app rebuilds the scene the next time you open it, keeping your program, your view and the guide’s progress, so the reference solution always does what the level says it does.

The machine

What the dispenser says and wants

SignalDirectionMeaning
ReadyinWeb loaded, no fault, roller home. The only time an Apply is any use
ApplyoutDrive the roller in. Hold it until PadIn; on a real FLS the stroke aborts if Apply drops early
PadIninThe roller is at the end of its stroke: the label has been pressed on. Drop Apply now
LabeledinThe bottle under the roller carries a label
Label_PresentinA label is peeled and waiting at the dispensing edge
Label_LowinFive labels or fewer on the roll
ErrorinThe roll is out, or the last cycle found no label. Stays on until a new roll is loaded (click the labeler)

Two things are easy to miss. Labeled is about the bottle under the roller, not the one at the pusher two metres on, so a verdict has to be carried down the belt in a bit of your own. And an uncapped bottle is not an error: with Only label capped bottles on the dispenser cycles, finds no cap, logs a skip and leaves the bottle alone, so after PadIn the bottle still reads Labeled = 0, and that is how the program knows it has to go to the reject bin.

How the level is scored

What happensPoints
A labeled, capped bottle in Good_Bin+100
An uncapped bottle in Reject_Bin+100
A bottle in Good_Bin with no label or no cap−100
A labeled bottle in Reject_Bin−50
Every Apply with no bottle under the roller, at the end−25 each
Every cycle on an empty roll, at the end−25 each
Under par (75 s)+200

How to pass it, step by step

1. Release one bottle at a time, and none while Error is on: a bottle sent into a dry dispenser is a cycle

2. Stop the belt when PE_Label sees a bottle that has no label yet. Let it settle.

3. Wait for Ready, then latch Apply. Unlatch it on PadIn (or on Error).

4. After PadIn, if the bottle still has no label, remember it: that one is for the pusher.

5. With the roller home, let the bottle go. Release the next one as soon as this one has left the eye: the trips

6. At PE_Reject, push the remembered bottle while the eye sees it; let the rest run on.

7. Amber on Label_Low, red on Error. The operator loads a new roll a few seconds after the red lamp;

Tags this lesson needs

The alias tags of the machine are made for you; create these before you type the rungs. Verify reports any you miss.

TagTypeKindDescription

Lamp_RedBOOLalias of Local:4:O.Data.8Red lamp: roll out, load a new one

Run and release

Rung 2 is the one that keeps the level honest: XIO(Error) in the release. Leave it out and the hopper keeps feeding bottles into a dispenser that cannot label them; each one costs 25 at the end and goes to Good_Bin bare for another 100. Rung 3 runs the belt unless a bottle is being held.

Hold, dwell and the Apply handshake

Rung 4 latches Hold for a bottle at the eye with no label, and XIO(Done) keeps it from re-latching for the same bottle once the dispenser has had its turn. Rung 5 is a 0.3 s dwell so the bottle has stopped moving before the roller touches it. Rung 6 is the request: held, settled, Ready, and not already done: latch Apply. Rung 7 is the answer: PadIn unlatches it, and so does Error, which is what the dispenser does with a cycle that finds no label.

Watch for: apply as an ote

Write rung 6 with an OTE instead of a latch and the roller never gets there. The moment it leaves home Ready drops (the dispenser is cycling), the rung goes false, Apply drops, the roller comes back, Ready returns, and it starts again: a roller twitching at the bottle. A latch set on Ready and cleared on PadIn is the shape of every start/acknowledge handshake in this book, the servo axis’s Start included.

The verdict, and letting the bottle go

Rung 8 runs on PadIn: it marks the bottle Done, and if Labeled is still off it latches No_Label, the verdict that rides down to the pusher. Rung 9 releases the hold once the roller is home. Rung 10 clears Done and Busy when the bottle has left the eye, so the next release goes out while this bottle is still on its way to the pusher. Rung 11 counts labels.

Try it: what the skip looks like

Run the level and watch the Simulator Log for Labeler skipped an open bottle. Find that bottle in Monitor Tags: at PadIn, Labeled stays 0 and No_Label comes on; two seconds later Reject fires at the pusher and the log says → Reject_Bin (no cap, no label) 100. Now set the labeler’s Only label capped bottles off and run again: the roller puts a label on the open bottle, the pusher lets it through, and Good_Bin charges 100 for a bottle shipped with no cap. The property is there because a real line rejects an open bottle before it wastes a label on it.

The pusher and the lamps

Rung 12 is Level 7’s pattern: on the eye’s rising edge, arm Fire from the verdict and forget the verdict; rung 13 pushes while the eye sees the bottle; rung 14 disarms when it is clear. The one-shot matters: without it rung 12 would clear No_Label in the same scan it read it, and the push would last one scan.

Try it: run the roll out

Run with the reference. Around bottle 19 LOW lights (five left). At the twentieth capped bottle the roller comes in and nothing goes on: Error comes on, Apply is unlatched by rung 7, the red lamp lights, and rung 2 stops the hopper. The bottle under the roller waits. Click the labeler: a new roll of 16 labels loaded, Error drops, Ready returns, rung 6 fires again and that bottle gets its label; the hopper carries on. Now take XIO(Error) out of rung 2 and watch what the hopper does while the roll is out.

Run it

Load the program, Run mode, Start. The first bottle stops at the eye, the roller comes in and back, the bottle runs on to Good_Bin and the next one is already on its way. The fourth or fifth is an open one: the roller comes in, nothing goes on, and the pusher takes it two metres later.

Part VI — Beyond the bottle line

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: RUN: Start seals Run in; Stop or a tripped E-stop breaks it

pred.q: Start_PB is off, Run is on, Stop_PB is off and E_Stop is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on) or (Run (Line running (sealed-in Start)) is on), Stop_PB (Stop push button, momentary) is off and E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB is off.
  3. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  4. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.words: When Run (Line running (sealed-in Start)) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Run (Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 2
rungs.comment: RELEASE one bottle at a time, and none while the dispenser is in Error: with the roll out, a released bottle would only reach a roller that cannot label it
rungs.words: When Run (Line running (sealed-in Start)) is on, Infeed_Ready (Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released) is on, Busy (A bottle is on the belt between the hopper and the labeler) is off, Error (Labeler: end of roll, or a cycle with no label) is off and this is the first scan of it, the rung turns Infeed_Release (Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false) and latches Busy on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(Infeed_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Infeed_Ready is on.
  3. XIO(Busy) Examine If Open asks: true when Busy is off.
  4. XIO(Error) Examine If Open asks: true when Error is off.
  5. ONS(Rel_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rel_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  6. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Infeed_Release) Output Energize does: turns Infeed_Release on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTL(Busy) Output Latch does: latches Busy on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Busy stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: BELT: runs unless a bottle is being held at the labeler
rungs.words: When Run (Line running (sealed-in Start)) is on and Hold (The belt is held with a bottle at the labeler) is off, the rung turns Conveyor_Run (Belt motor) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Hold) Examine If Open asks: true when Hold is off.
  3. OTE(Conveyor_Run) Output Energize does: turns Conveyor_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: HOLD: a bottle at the labeler's eye with no label yet, and not one the dispenser has already dealt with: stop it under the roller

pred.q: PE_Label is off, Labeled is off and Done is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Hold is left as it was. It stops at XIC(PE_Label).

rungs.words: When PE_Label (A bottle is under the labeler's roller) is on, Labeled (Labeler: the bottle under the roller carries a label) is off and Done (The dispenser has had its turn at the bottle under the roller) is off, the rung latches Hold (The belt is held with a bottle at the labeler) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Label) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Label is on.
  2. XIO(Labeled) Examine If Open asks: true when Labeled is off.
  3. XIO(Done) Examine If Open asks: true when Done is off.
  4. OTL(Hold) Output Latch does: latches Hold on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Hold stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: DWELL: let the bottle settle for 0.3 s before the roller comes in
rungs.words: When Hold (The belt is held with a bottle at the labeler) is on, the rung runs the timer Dwell (Time for the bottle to settle at the eye before Apply) toward 300 ms.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Hold) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hold is on.
  2. TON(Dwell,300,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Dwell toward 300 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Dwell counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 6
rungs.comment: APPLY: the bottle is held and the dispenser is Ready (web loaded, no fault, roller home): drive the roller in. Latched, so it stays in until the stroke ends

pred.q: Hold is on, Dwell.DN is on, Ready is on and Done is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Apply latches on.

rungs.words: When Hold (The belt is held with a bottle at the labeler) is on, Dwell.DN (the done bit of Dwell: Time for the bottle to settle at the eye before Apply) is on, Ready (Labeler: web loaded, no fault, not cycling) is on and Done (The dispenser has had its turn at the bottle under the roller) is off, the rung latches Apply (Labeler: drive the roller in against the bottle (hold until PadIn)) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Hold) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hold is on.
  2. XIC(Dwell.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Dwell.DN is on.
  3. XIC(Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Ready is on.
  4. XIO(Done) Examine If Open asks: true when Done is off.
  5. OTL(Apply) Output Latch does: latches Apply on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Apply stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 7
rungs.comment: PAD IN: the roller is at the end of its stroke and the label is on: let the roller back. An Error drops it too
rungs.words: When either (PadIn (Labeler: roller at the end of its stroke, the label is pressed on) is on) or (Error (Labeler: end of roll, or a cycle with no label) is on), the rung unlatches Apply (Labeler: drive the roller in against the bottle (hold until PadIn)).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(PadIn) Examine If Closed asks: true when PadIn is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Error) Examine If Closed asks: true when Error is on.
  2. OTU(Apply) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Apply. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Apply when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 8
rungs.comment: DONE: the roller has been in. If the bottle still has no label it had no cap (Only label capped bottles is on): remember that for the pusher

pred.q: Hold is off, PadIn is off and Labeled is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Done is left as it was and No_Label is left as it was. It stops at XIC(Hold).

rungs.words: When Hold (The belt is held with a bottle at the labeler) is on and PadIn (Labeler: roller at the end of its stroke, the label is pressed on) is on, each path is tested on its own: it latches Done (The dispenser has had its turn at the bottle under the roller) on; if Labeled (Labeler: the bottle under the roller carries a label) is off, it latches No_Label (The bottle on its way to the pusher left the labeler with no label (no cap)) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Hold) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hold is on.
  2. XIC(PadIn) Examine If Closed asks: true when PadIn is on.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(Done) Output Latch does: latches Done on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Labeled) Examine If Open asks: true when Labeled is off.
    2. OTL(No_Label) Output Latch does: latches No_Label on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Done stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 9
rungs.comment: GO: the dispenser has had its turn and the roller is home: let the bottle go
rungs.words: When Done (The dispenser has had its turn at the bottle under the roller) is on, Apply (Labeler: drive the roller in against the bottle (hold until PadIn)) is off and PadIn (Labeler: roller at the end of its stroke, the label is pressed on) is off, the rung unlatches Hold (The belt is held with a bottle at the labeler).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Done) Examine If Closed asks: true when Done is on.
  2. XIO(Apply) Examine If Open asks: true when Apply is off.
  3. XIO(PadIn) Examine If Open asks: true when PadIn is off.
  4. OTU(Hold) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Hold. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Hold when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 10
rungs.comment: CLEAR: once the bottle has left the eye the next one is a new job, and the hopper can release it: the trips overlap

pred.q: Done is on and PE_Label is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Done is unlatched and Busy is unlatched.

rungs.words: When Done (The dispenser has had its turn at the bottle under the roller) is on and PE_Label (A bottle is under the labeler's roller) is off, the rung unlatches Done and unlatches Busy (A bottle is on the belt between the hopper and the labeler).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Done) Examine If Closed asks: true when Done is on.
  2. XIO(PE_Label) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Label is off.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Done) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Done. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Busy) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Busy. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Done when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 11
rungs.comment: COUNT each bottle as it is labeled
rungs.words: When Labeled (Labeler: the bottle under the roller carries a label) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung makes Label_Count (Shown on the toolbar: bottles labeled) = Label_Count + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Labeled) Examine If Closed asks: true when Labeled is on.
  2. ONS(Cnt_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Cnt_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. ADD(Label_Count,1,Label_Count) Add does: makes Label_Count = Label_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 12
rungs.comment: AT THE PUSHER: if the bottle left the labeler with no label, arm the pusher; either way forget the verdict
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (A bottle is at the reject pusher) is on and this is the first scan of it, each path is tested on its own: if No_Label (The bottle on its way to the pusher left the labeler with no label (no cap)) is on, it latches Fire (The bottle at the pusher is to be rejected) on; it unlatches No_Label.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(Rej_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rej_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(No_Label) Examine If Closed asks: true when No_Label is on.
    2. OTL(Fire) Output Latch does: latches Fire on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(No_Label) Output Unlatch does: unlatches No_Label. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: Fire stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 13
rungs.comment: REJECT: push while the eye sees the bottle, until it is in Reject_Bin
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (A bottle is at the reject pusher) is on and Fire (The bottle at the pusher is to be rejected) is on, the rung turns Reject (Reject pusher: push the bottle into Reject_Bin) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. XIC(Fire) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fire is on.
  3. OTE(Reject) Output Energize does: turns Reject on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 14
rungs.comment: disarm once the pusher's eye is clear

pred.q: PE_Reject is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Fire is left as it was. It stops at XIO(PE_Reject).

rungs.words: When PE_Reject (A bottle is at the reject pusher) is off, the rung unlatches Fire (The bottle at the pusher is to be rejected).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(PE_Reject) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Reject is off.
  2. OTU(Fire) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fire. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Fire when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 15
rungs.comment: LABELS LOW: the amber lamp tells the operator to have a roll ready
rungs.words: When Label_Low (Labeler: 5 labels or fewer on the roll) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Amber (Amber lamp: labels low) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Label_Low) Examine If Closed asks: true when Label_Low is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Amber) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Amber on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 16
rungs.comment: ROLL OUT: the red lamp: load a new roll (click the labeler). Error clears with it and the line carries on

pred.q: Error is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Lamp_Red is on.

rungs.words: When Error (Labeler: end of roll, or a cycle with no label) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Red (Red lamp: roll out, load a new one) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Error) Examine If Closed asks: true when Error is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Red) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Red on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

Infeed_Ready.desc: Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released

Busy.desc: A bottle is on the belt between the hopper and the labeler

Error.desc: Labeler: end of roll, or a cycle with no label

Infeed_Release.desc: Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)

Hold.desc: The belt is held with a bottle at the labeler

PE_Label.desc: A bottle is under the labeler's roller

Labeled.desc: Labeler: the bottle under the roller carries a label

Done.desc: The dispenser has had its turn at the bottle under the roller

Dwell.desc: Time for the bottle to settle at the eye before Apply

Ready.desc: Labeler: web loaded, no fault, not cycling

Apply.desc: Labeler: drive the roller in against the bottle (hold until PadIn)

PadIn.desc: Labeler: roller at the end of its stroke, the label is pressed on

No_Label.desc: The bottle on its way to the pusher left the labeler with no label (no cap)

Label_Count.desc: Shown on the toolbar: bottles labeled

PE_Reject.desc: A bottle is at the reject pusher

Fire.desc: The bottle at the pusher is to be rejected

Reject.desc: Reject pusher: push the bottle into Reject_Bin

Label_Low.desc: Labeler: 5 labels or fewer on the roll

Lamp_Red.desc: Red lamp: roll out, load a new one
